newsitem.title: FRANCE: Big guns destroyed in Bosnia and Serbia.
newsitem.headline: Big guns destroyed in Bosnia and Serbia.

text.p: France and Germany began a joint operation this week to destroy large quantities of heavy weapons in Bosnia and Serbia under year-old Balkans disarmament accords, the French foreign ministry said on Wednesday.
Under the operation due to end in October, 800 artillery pieces, 150 tanks and 20 armoured vehicles in Serbia and 700 guns in the Bosnia-Herzegovina federation will be rendered useless.
Gun barrels will be cut off, and tank turrets and engines irreversibly damaged. Forty percent of the weapons will be destroyed by July 14, with the rest following between September 15 and October 31.
France and Germany will provide equal quantities of blowlamp gas for a total cost of 200,000 francs ($38,000), as well as a joint team of army officers and technicians to monitor the destruction.

The French ministry said that 1,700 heavy weapons had already been destroyed since the agreement, which also involves Croatia, was signed a year ago in Florence. More than 3,500 remain to be destroyed by October.

It said the disarmament agreement was being implemented fairy smoothly after some problems were overcome at the end of last year. The international community was closely checking that none of the former warring parties was hiding any heavy weapon.

NATO contributors to a NATO-led force in Bosnia fear that, unless peace accords are implemented in full, the Balkan country could slip back into war after foreign troops leave as scheduled in June 1998.
